A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SwiReasoning framework. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning accuracy, token-efficiency, Pass@k, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds larger-model and broader-domain evaluations, runtime measurements, diagnostic analyses, and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same entropy-based switching, asymmetric dwell windows, signal mixing, and convergence/termination controller. New ablation variants test components without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 retains the five mathematics/STEM benchmarks and adds coding on HumanEval, LeetCode-Contest, MBPP, and LiveCodeBench; multi-hop QA on LongBench's 2WikiMultihopQA; and commonsense reasoning on CommonsenseQA (Appendix C.3). This substantially broadens evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: Sampled CoT, greedy CoT, and Soft Thinking remain the external comparators, including in the new benchmark evaluations. v2 additionally evaluates controller-retaining SwiR without latent reasoning and component-removal/symmetric-window variants as ablation comparators (Tables 8–9).

E3.justification: Original evaluation settings remain unchanged. New protocols add Qwen3-32B evaluation, latency/TFLOP comparisons at fixed accuracy, entropy and top-five embedding-similarity diagnostics, and controlled trigger/window/component variations. Appendix C.4 labels its runtime model 'Qwen-3B' without resolving its precise identity.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's window-size, mixing-coefficient, and budget analyses, v2 adds exploration diagnostics, switch-count distributions by difficulty, a spatial-reasoning failure case, convergence-timing tests, and controls isolating latent reasoning and window asymmetry/removal (C.1 and C.5–C.9). Some original window and budget results are reused, but the additional controls address previously untested questions.

E5.justification: Figure 8 newly reports descriptive variability through switch-count boxplots, medians, and ranges across problems. This concerns problem-level variation, not repeated-run accuracy uncertainty. The eight-repeat AIME averaging statement remains unchanged; no new seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results: Qwen3-32B averages of 84.30% for SwiR versus 82.38% for CoT, broader-domain averages of 81.24% versus 78.54%, and runtime, diagnostic, and ablation findings. These are newly reported evaluations. Original main results and all detailed rows in v1 Tables 5–19 are retained in v2 Tables 11–25.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of latent embeddings, switching, signal mixing, controller behavior, and token efficiency are unchanged. The added empirical diagnostics and illustrated erroneous model solution introduce no new theoretical result, proof, or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free mode switching, overthinking suppression, accuracy, and token efficiency. The additional appendix evidence does not revise these main claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning difficulty-adaptive switching, latent reasoning's contribution beyond stopping control, and convergence-timing tradeoffs. Appendix C.6 introduces rigid geometric constraints as a specific failure condition and attributes the example's error to latent smoothing; that causal explanation remains tentative evidence from one case.

D1.justification: v2 documents how the top-five embedding-similarity diagnostic is calculated, how the explicit-only ablation retains stopping triggers, and which switch caps correspond to reported accuracy/length pairs. Algorithm 1, Table 4, and listed code/data links remain unchanged. Hardware and timing implementation details are still unspecified.

R1.justification: New references support the added coding and QA benchmarks. Appendix B.4 also explicitly discusses COCONUT and Long⊗Short as training-based efficiency approaches. The central positioning as a training-free alternative to purely latent reasoning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are almost unchanged, with limited citation, bibliographic, and cross-reference edits. Appendix C gains organized subsections C.1–C.9, while its original detailed-results subsection becomes C.10; existing prose undergoes little rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with Figures 6–8, Tables 5–10, and a boxed, annotated reasoning trace spanning two pages. These include diagnostic curves, latency/compute plots, switch-count boxplots, and comparison/ablation tables. Original figures remain unchanged, and original appendix tables are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support for the paper. The controller-retaining explicit-only comparison in Table 8 addresses whether latent reasoning contributes beyond early stopping, while new component controls, broader tasks, and Qwen3-32B evaluation strengthen mechanism assessment and generality. Runtime measurements and a concrete failure analysis add practical perspective. The timing setup remains underspecified and the failure's causal attribution is tentative, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains over v1.
